桌上有一根针，想让它从朝右变成朝左。最直白的办法：按住中点转半圈——能掉头，但针: A needle on the table should face left instead of right. The plainest way: pin its midpoint and spin half a turn—it works, but the needle sweeps a whole disk: π/4 ≈ 0.785.
换个支点，立省一成: Move the pivot, save a tenth
别绕中点转。把针尖轮流挂在等边三角形的三个角上，各抡 60°，三次正好掉头。扫过: Don’t spin around the midpoint. Hang the needle’s tip on each corner of an equilateral triangle in turn, swinging 60° each time—three swings complete the turn. The swept shape is a Reuleaux triangle: (π−√3)/2 ≈ 0.705.
1917 年，挂谷宗一想出一条更绝的轨道：小圆贴着三倍大的圆内壁滚一圈，笔尖就描: In 1917, Sōichi Kakeya found a subtler track: roll a small circle inside one three times its size, and the pen tip traces this three-cusped deltoid.
贴着弧滑，面积砍半: Slide along the arcs, halve the area
这条曲线的神妙之处：任意切线卡在弧里的那段，永远刚好一根针长。针贴壁滑过半圈就掉: The magic of this curve: any tangent clipped by the arcs is always exactly one needle long. Sliding halfway along the wall completes the turn, sweeping π/8 ≈ 0.393—exactly half the disk. Kakeya guessed this was the minimum.
这个猜想撑了十年。把三角形切成越来越细的条，再平移推拢——平移不改变方向，扇面里: The conjecture held for a decade. Slice the triangle into ever thinner strips and slide them together—translation changes no direction, so the fan keeps every direction, yet the combined area drops round after round.
细条之间，蹭着换轨: Brush and switch between the strips
细条被推到互相重叠：针滑进重叠区，小转几度，再滑进下一条。一片细条管 60° 扇: The strips are pushed into overlap: the needle slides into an overlap, turns a few degrees, slides into the next. One bundle covers a 60° fan; three take turns for the full 180°. Cut finer, and the total area shrinks below any bound.
面积可以逼近零，维度却塌不下去——它仍要向四面八方铺开。这就是挂谷猜想；2025: The area can approach zero, but the dimension cannot collapse—it must still spread in every direction. That is the Kakeya conjecture; in 2025, Wang and Zahl proved the three-dimensional case.
